name: 新概念英语第二册风格
desc: 仿《新概念英语2》风格：97 个高频核心词 + 12 篇幽默短篇故事（约 100–150 词，一般过去时叙事 + 结尾妙句）+ 计划任务库。课文为原创，规避版权。
descEn: Book-2-style pack: 97 core words + 12 original humorous short stories (~100–150 words, past-tense narrative with punchline endings) + plan task bank. Original texts, copyright-safe.

words.defEn: belonging to one person only; not public
words.ex: He keeps his diary in a private drawer.
words.exzh: 他把日记放在私人抽屉里。
words.exEn: He keeps his diary in a drawer nobody else opens.

words.ex: We had a long conversation about the film.
words.exzh: 我们就那部电影聊了很久。
words.exEn: We talked about the film for a long time.

words.defEn: a building where plays are performed
words.ex: The theatre was full last night.
words.exEn: The playhouse was crowded last night.

words.ex: I found my seat in the third row.
words.exzh: 我在第三排找到了座位。
words.exEn: I found the place where I sat in row three.

words.ex: The play began at eight o'clock.
words.exEn: The performance started at eight.

words.defEn: in a way that makes much noise
words.ex: Someone was coughing loudly behind us.
words.exzh: 有人在我们身后大声咳嗽。
words.exEn: Someone behind us was coughing noisily.

words.ex: She got angry when the bus left early.
words.exzh: 公交车提前开走时她很生气。
words.exEn: She became cross when the bus went too soon.

words.defEn: to tolerate; to put up with
words.ex: I can't bear the noise any longer.
words.exzh: 我再也受不了这噪音了。
words.exEn: I cannot stand the noise anymore.

words.ex: It's none of your business.
words.exEn: It does not concern you.

words.ex: The waiter spoke rudely to the old man.
words.exzh: 侍者对老人说话很无礼。
words.exEn: The waiter was impolite to the old man.

words.defEn: to leave a vehicle in a place
words.ex: You can't park here — it's a bus stop.
words.exzh: 这里不能停车——这是公交站。
words.exEn: You must not leave your car here.

words.defEn: the movement of vehicles on roads
words.ex: The traffic was heavy this morning.
words.exEn: There were many cars on the road this morning.

words.defEn: a printed note of fine; pass for entry
words.ex: The officer gave him a ticket for parking.
words.exzh: 交警因违停给他开了罚单。
words.exEn: The officer fined him for leaving his car there.

words.ex: I left a note on the kitchen table.
words.exzh: 我在餐桌上留了张便条。
words.exEn: I wrote a short message and left it on the table.

words.defEn: a particular part of a place or city
words.ex: This area is quiet at night.
words.exEn: This part of town is calm after dark.

words.ex: Didn't you see the 'No Parking' sign?
words.exzh: 你没看到“禁止停车”的标志吗？
words.exEn: Did you not notice the board?

words.ex: Please remind me to call her at six.
words.exzh: 请提醒我六点给她打电话。
words.exEn: Help me remember to phone her at six.

words.ex: Good luck brought them together again.
words.exEn: Fortune brought them back together.

words.defEn: to take and use something that will be returned
words.ex: May I borrow your umbrella?
words.exEn: Can I use your umbrella for a while?

words.ex: One late train spoiled our whole plan.
words.exzh: 一班车晚点毁了我们整个计划。
words.exEn: One delayed train ruined our plans.

words.defEn: a place where old things are shown
words.ex: The museum closes at five o'clock.
words.exEn: The exhibition hall shuts at five.

words.ex: The weather was terrible yesterday.
words.exEn: Yesterday's weather was awful.

words.ex: Smoking is banned in public places.
words.exEn: No smoking where everyone goes.

words.ex: It was a hard decision to make.
words.exEn: Choosing was difficult.

words.ex: The whole class passed the exam.
words.exEn: Everyone in class passed the test.

words.ex: He answered my letter immediately.
words.exEn: He replied at once.

words.defEn: feeling pleased about something done well
words.ex: She was proud of her son's progress.
words.exzh: 她为儿子的进步感到自豪。
words.exEn: Her son's progress pleased her greatly.

words.ex: Sleep is important for memory.
words.exEn: Sleep matters greatly for remembering.

words.ex: To my surprise, the door was open.
words.exEn: Unexpectedly, the door stood open.

words.ex: The market was crowded on Sunday.
words.exEn: Sunday's market was packed with people.

words.ex: He refused to give up his seat.
words.exEn: He would not give up his seat.

words.defEn: to say you are not satisfied
words.ex: Customers complained about the long wait.
words.exEn: Customers said they waited far too long.

words.defEn: to get something useful or wanted
words.ex: He gained experience working abroad.
words.exzh: 他在国外工作获得了经验。
words.exEn: Working abroad gave him experience.

words.ex: Excuse me for interrupting you.
words.exEn: Forgive me for stopping your speech.

words.ex: The factory employs two hundred workers.
words.exzh: 这家工厂雇了两百名工人。
words.exEn: Two hundred workers are paid by the factory.

words.ex: He saves half of his salary every month.
words.exEn: Each month he saves half his pay.

words.ex: I still owe him ten dollars.
words.exEn: I must still return ten dollars to him.

words.ex: What a pity you missed the show!
words.exEn: How sad that you missed it!

words.ex: She entertained us with funny stories.
words.exzh: 她用有趣的故事招待我们。
words.exEn: Her funny stories amused us all.

words.ex: They stayed in a charming little hotel.
words.exzh: 他们住进一家迷人的小旅馆。
words.exEn: Their little hotel was delightful.

words.ex: I didn't recognize her new hairstyle.
words.exEn: I could not tell who she was at first.

words.ex: He suggested going out for dinner.
words.exEn: He put forward the idea of dinner out.

words.ex: Wet floors are a hazard for old people.
words.exzh: 湿地板对老人是种危险。
words.exEn: Wet floors endanger older people.

words.defEn: what you see at a place
words.ex: Police arrived quickly at the scene.
words.exEn: Officers reached the spot fast.

words.ex: His first attempt failed, but he tried again.
words.exzh: 第一次尝试失败后他又试了。
words.exEn: His first try failed, yet he tried once more.

words.ex: Firemen rescued the cat from the tree.
words.exzh: 消防员把猫从树上救下。
words.exEn: Firefighters saved the cat up the tree.

words.ex: Don't worry — the flight is on time.
words.exEn: Be at ease; the plane is punctual.

words.ex: Be patient; results take time.
words.exEn: Wait calmly; outcomes come slowly.

words.ex: Her memory amazed the doctors.
words.exzh: 她的记忆力让医生们惊讶。
words.exEn: Doctors were astonished by her memory.

words.defEn: cloth hung at a window or stage
words.ex: She drew the curtains before bed.
words.exEn: Before sleep she closed the window cloth.

words.defEn: to make known what was hidden
words.ex: The letter revealed an old secret.
words.exzh: 信中揭示了一个旧秘密。
words.exEn: The letter made an old secret known.

words.defEn: to come together in one place
words.ex: A crowd gathered around the singer.
words.exEn: People came together near the singer.

words.ex: The repair cost a considerable sum.
words.exzh: 修理花了一笔可观的钱。
words.exEn: Repairs took quite a large amount.

words.defEn: a part broken off; an item
words.ex: The vase fell to pieces.
words.exEn: The vase broke into many bits.

words.ex: Time is more precious than money.
words.exEn: Time is worth more than coins.

words.ex: They studied ancient Greek stories.
words.exEn: They read tales from long-gone Greece.

words.ex: Every culture has its own myths.
words.exzh: 每种文化都有自己的神话。
words.exEn: Each culture keeps ancient tales alive.

words.ex: He stayed out of trouble at school.
words.exEn: At school he caused no problems.

words.defEn: to get free from a place
words.ex: Two birds escaped from the cage.
words.exzh: 两只鸟从笼子里逃走了。
words.exEn: Two birds flew free from their cage.

words.defEn: arm of a tree; local office
words.ex: The cat sat on the highest branch.
words.exEn: The cat rested on the topmost arm of the tree.

words.ex: The box lost weight after we emptied it.
words.exEn: Once emptied, the box weighed less.

words.defEn: below the surface of the ground
words.ex: They traveled by underground railway.
words.exEn: They rode trains beneath the city.

words.ex: Steam rose from the hot soup.
words.exEn: Hot mist floated above the soup.

words.defEn: leader of a ship or team
words.ex: The captain guided us through the storm.
words.exzh: 船长带领我们穿过风暴。
words.exEn: Our leader steered us through rough seas.

words.ex: They sailed south along the coast.
words.exEn: They traveled southward by sea.

words.ex: Fishing boats returned to harbour at dusk.
words.exEn: Fishing boats came home as light faded.

words.defEn: very bad weather with wind and rain
words.ex: The storm kept us indoors all day.
words.exzh: 风暴让我们一整天待在室内。
words.exEn: Bad weather held us inside all day.

words.ex: Driving fast in rain is dangerous.
words.exEn: Speeding in rain can harm you.

words.ex: Morning exercise wakes up the body.
words.exEn: Moving each morning freshens you up.

words.ex: They secretly planned a birthday party.
words.exzh: 他们秘密筹划生日派对。
words.exEn: Quietly they planned the party unseen.

words.defEn: feeling ashamed in front of others
words.ex: He felt embarrassed singing in public.
words.exEn: Singing before others shamed him a little.

words.defEn: feeling one did wrong; judged wrong
words.ex: She felt guilty about forgetting his name.
words.exzh: 忘了他的名字让她很内疚。
words.exEn: Forgetting his name troubled her conscience.

words.ex: Our teacher is strict but fair.
words.exzh: 我们的老师严格但公正。
words.exEn: Our teacher demands much, yet treats all fairly.

words.ex: A kind word is its own reward.
words.exzh: 善意的话本身就是奖赏。
words.exEn: Kindness pays back in itself.

words.ex: Parents sacrifice sleep for babies.
words.exEn: Parents give up sleep so babies rest.

words.ex: Could you do me a favour and post this?
words.exzh: 能帮我个忙把这封信寄了吗？
words.exEn: Would you kindly mail this letter for me?

words.defEn: from a ship into the water
words.ex: A wave washed his hat overboard.
words.exzh: 一个浪头把他的帽子卷进了海里。
words.exEn: A big wave swept his hat into the sea.

words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.exzh: 他一头扎进冰冷的水里。
words.exEn: Into the icy water he dove at once.

words.ex: She struggled up the snowy hill.
words.exEn: With effort she climbed the snowy slope.

words.ex: The price rose slightly last month.
words.exEn: Prices edged up a little last month.

words.defEn: to see and become aware of
words.ex: Did you notice the new painting?
words.exzh: 你注意到那幅新画了吗？
words.exEn: Did you see the picture just hung?

words.ex: The road is temporarily closed.
words.exEn: For now the road stays shut.

words.ex: The actual trip took nine hours.
words.exEn: In fact the journey lasted nine hours.

words.ex: Our flight leaves at noon.
words.exEn: Our plane departs at midday.

words.ex: He showed extreme patience with children.
words.exzh: 他对孩子表现出极大的耐心。
words.exEn: His patience with children knew few limits.

words.ex: A large quantity of rice was stored here.
words.exEn: Much grain once filled this store.

words.defEn: to move goods secretly and illegally
words.ex: Customs officers caught men smuggling clocks.
words.exzh: 海关官员抓到偷运钟表的人。
words.exEn: Officers stopped men moving clocks unlawfully.

words.ex: An officious guard checked every bag twice.
words.exzh: 一个爱管事警卫把每个包查了两遍。
words.exEn: A bossy guard searched each bag twice over.

words.ex: He unscrewed the cap of the bottle.
words.exEn: Turning hard, he opened the bottle top.

words.ex: Traffic noise was dreadful downtown.
words.exzh: 市中心的交通噪音糟透了。
words.exEn: Downtown street noise was awful beyond words.

words.defEn: to cover a road with flat stones
words.ex: Workers paved the square with grey stones.
words.exEn: Grey stones covered the square anew.

words.defEn: a figure made of stone or metal
words.ex: Pigeons rested on the statue's head.
words.exzh: 鸽子停在雕像头上休息。
words.exEn: Birds perched upon the stone head.

words.ex: They erected a tent near the lake.
words.exEn: Near the water they raised a tent.

words.ex: Soon she grew accustomed to city noise.
words.exzh: 不久她习惯了城市噪音。
words.exEn: In time the city noise felt normal to her.

words.ex: Never skip breakfast before school.
words.exEn: Eat before class; never leave breakfast out.

words.defEn: to pause before acting from doubt
words.ex: Don't hesitate to ask questions.
words.exEn: Ask freely; doubt should not delay you.

words.ex: They intend to visit Xi'an next spring.
words.exzh: 他们打算明年春天去西安。
words.exEn: Next spring they plan to see Xi'an.

readings.title: 私人谈话
readings.text: Last week I went to the theatre. I had a very good seat. The play was very interesting. I did not enjoy it. A young man and a young woman were sitting behind me. They were talking loudly. I got very angry. I could not hear the actors. I turned round. I looked at the man and the woman angrily. They did not pay any attention. In the end, I could not bear it. I turned round again. "It's none of your business," the young man said rudely. "This is a private conversation!"

questions.q: Where did the writer go last week?
Why couldn't the writer enjoy the play?
options: Two people were talking loudly behind him

questions.q: What did the young man mean by 'a private conversation'?
options: It was none of the writer's business

readings.title: 早餐还是午餐？
readings.text: It was Sunday. I never get up early on Sundays. I sometimes stay in bed until lunchtime. Last Sunday I got up very late. I looked out of the window. It was dark outside. "What a day!" I thought. "It's raining again." Just then, the telephone rang. It was my aunt Lucy. "I've just arrived by train," she said. "I'm coming to see you." "But I'm still having breakfast," I said. "What are you doing?" she asked. "I'm having breakfast," I repeated. "Dear me," she said. "Do you always get up so late? It's one o'clock!"

questions.q: When does the writer usually stay in bed until?
Who telephoned the writer?
What time was it really?

readings.title: 请给我寄张明信片
readings.text: Postcards always spoil my holidays. Last summer, I went to Italy. I visited museums and sat in public gardens. A friendly waiter taught me a few words of Italian. Then he lent me a book. I read a few lines, but I did not understand a word. Every day I thought about postcards. My holidays passed quickly, but I did not send cards to my friends. On the last day I made a big decision. I got up early and bought thirty-seven cards. I spent the whole day in my room, but I did not write a single card!

questions.q: What always spoils the writer's holidays?
How many cards did the writer buy?
How many cards did he write?

readings.title: 激动人心的旅行
readings.text: I have just received a letter from my brother, Tim. He is in Australia. He has been there for six months. Tim is an engineer. He is working for a big firm and he has already visited a great number of different places in Australia. He has just bought an Australian car and has gone to Alice Springs, a small town in the centre of Australia. He will soon visit Darwin. From there, he will fly to Perth. My brother has never been abroad before, so he is finding this trip very exciting.

questions.q: What is Tim's job?
Where is Alice Springs?
Why does Tim find the trip exciting?
options: It is his first time abroad

readings.title: 无错号之娱
readings.text: Joe Sanders has the most beautiful garden in our town. Nearly everybody enters for 'The Nicest Garden Competition' each year, but Joe wins every time. Bill Frith's garden is larger than Joe's. Bill works harder than Joe and grows more flowers and vegetables, but Joe's garden is more interesting. He has made neat paths and has built a wooden bridge over a pool. I like gardens too, but I do not like hard work. Every year I enter for the garden competition too, and I always win a little prize for the worst garden in the town!

questions.q: Whose garden is larger?
Why does Joe win every year?
options: His garden is the most beautiful

questions.q: What prize does the writer win?

readings.title: 又是一个星期天
readings.text: I was having dinner at a restaurant when Tony Steele came in. Tony worked in a lawyer's office years ago, but he is now working at a bank. He gets a good salary, but he always borrows money from his friends and never pays it back. Tony saw me and came and sat at the same table. He has never borrowed money from me. While he was eating, I asked him to lend me twenty pounds. To my surprise, he gave me the money immediately. "I have never borrowed any money from you," Tony said, "so now you can pay for my dinner!"

questions.q: Where does Tony work now?
What did the writer ask Tony?
Why did Tony hand over the money?
options: So the writer would pay for his dinner

readings.title: 警察与赞美诗式的小偷
readings.text: The plane was late and detectives were waiting at the airport all morning. They were expecting a valuable parcel of diamonds from South Africa. A few hours earlier, someone had told the police that thieves would try to steal the diamonds. When the plane arrived, some of the detectives were waiting inside the main building while others were waiting on the airfield. Two men took the parcel off the plane and carried it into the Customs House. While two detectives were keeping guard at the door, two others opened the parcel. To their surprise, the precious parcel was full of stones and sand!

questions.q: What were the detectives expecting?
Where was the parcel taken?
What did the parcel really contain?

readings.title: 卡塞特街11号
readings.text: I was walking along the street when I saw a crowd gathered outside a shop. A young man had just tried to steal a woman's handbag, but she held it firmly. The thief pulled hard, the strap snapped, and he ran off with the bag. A moment later everyone shouted: the woman's husband, a tall sailor, raced after him. He caught the thief in two minutes, carried him back by the collar, and handed both bag and thief to a policeman. Then he gave the bag to his wife — and asked her politely to buy him a cold drink as a reward.

questions.q: What did the thief try to steal?
Who caught the thief?
What reward did the sailor ask for?

readings.title: 冷遇
readings.titleEn: Do You Call That a Hat?
readings.text: "Do you call that a hat?" I said to my wife. "You needn't be so rude about it," my wife answered as she looked at herself in the mirror. I sat down on one of the modern easy-chairs. I had sat down only seconds when a voice at the door said, "Would you mind not sitting in that chair? It's for exhibition only." "I'm sorry," I said. "I didn't notice it." Our new furniture had arrived that morning, and everything in the living room was new — including the chairs people must not sit in.

questions.q: What did the writer criticize?
Why could he not sit in the chair?
When had the furniture arrived?

readings.title: 并非很懂音乐
readings.text: As we had had a long walk through one of the markets of Old Delhi, we stopped at a square to have a rest. After a time, we noticed a snake charmer with two large baskets at the other side of the square, so we went to have a look at him. As soon as he saw us, he picked up a long pipe which was covered with coins and opened one of the baskets. When he began to play a tune, we had our first glimpse of the snake. It rose out of the basket and began to follow the movements of the pipe. We were very surprised when the snake charmer suddenly began to play jazz and pop songs. The snake, however, continued to 'dance' slowly. It obviously could not tell the difference between Indian music and jazz!

questions.q: Why did they stop at the square?
What covered the pipe?
What surprised the visitors?

readings.title: 越过峡谷
readings.text: I love travelling in the country, but I don't like losing my way. I went on an excursion recently, but my trip took me longer than I expected. "I'm going to Woodford Green," I said to the conductor as I got on the bus, "but I don't know where it is." "I'll tell you where to get off," answered the conductor. I sat in the front of the bus to get a good view of the countryside. Some people on the bus watched the scenery, others read their papers. An old lady got off halfway — at a small bridge over a stream. "This isn't Woodford Green, is it?" I asked anxiously. "Oh dear!" said the conductor suddenly. "I forgot to put you off." "It doesn't matter," I said. "I'll get off here." "We're going back now," said the conductor. "Well, in that case, I prefer to stay on the bus," I answered.

questions.q: Where did the writer want to go?
What mistake did the conductor make?
options: Forgot to put the writer off

questions.q: Why did the writer stay on the bus?

readings.title: 绿林好汉式的海关
readings.text: I had an amusing experience last year. After I had left a small village in the south of France, I drove on to the next town. On the way, a young man waved to me. I stopped and he asked me for a lift. As soon as he had got into the car, I said good morning to him in French and he replied in the same language. Apart from a few words, I do not know any French at all. Neither of us spoke during the journey. I had nearly reached the town, when the young man suddenly said, very slowly, "Do you speak English?" As I soon learnt, he was English himself!

questions.q: Where did this happen?
What language did the writer use first?
What was surprising about the young man?
